title: Expressions, Variables & Translating Relationships
coreInsight: Algebraic symbols represent quantities and relationships; an expression describes a calculation, while an equation claims that two expressions are equal.
narrativeTransition: Take a repeated verbal relationship and give the changing or unknown quantity a name so the structure can be manipulated without rewriting the story.
commonMisconceptions: A variable is merely a label for an object.
A variable always represents exactly one mystery number.
Expressions and equations are interchangeable.
The equal sign means 'the answer comes next' rather than 'these quantities are equal'.

title: Linear Equations
coreInsight: Solving an equation means finding values that make a statement true, and valid transformations preserve equality.
narrativeTransition: Once a relationship is represented symbolically, ask which value makes the two sides balance and preserve that balance through every move.
commonMisconceptions: Terms can be moved across the equal sign by changing their sign without justification.
The variable's value changes during the solving process.
Different operations may be applied to the two sides of an equation.
A solution does not need to be checked in the original relationship.

title: Systems of Equations
coreInsight: Several unknown quantities can be determined when several independent constraints must hold simultaneously.
narrativeTransition: Use a situation in which one equation leaves many possibilities, then add a second independent observation that collapses the possibilities to one.
commonMisconceptions: One equation usually determines two unknown quantities.
A variable can take a different value in each equation of the same system.
Elimination is symbol manipulation unrelated to preserving the same solution set.
Finding one plausible pair is enough without checking every constraint.

title: Inequalities, Bounds & Optimization
coreInsight: Many problems ask for a range of feasible values or an extreme feasible value rather than one exact equality.
narrativeTransition: Replace 'equals' with 'at least' or 'at most' and let the set of possible solutions appear on a number line before optimizing within it.
commonMisconceptions: An inequality has one numerical answer.
Endpoint inclusion does not matter.
Equation rules can be copied blindly when multiplying or dividing by negatives.
Optimization can ignore feasibility constraints.

title: Functions & Defined Operations
coreInsight: A function or defined operation is a rule that transforms inputs; unfamiliar notation becomes manageable once the rule is followed consistently.
narrativeTransition: Turn an expression rule into a reusable machine, then nest machines so the learner must think input-to-output rather than by visual familiarity with symbols.
commonMisconceptions: f(x) means f multiplied by x.
A newly defined symbol keeps its ordinary arithmetic meaning.
Nested functions should be evaluated from the outside inward.
A function is only a formula, not a mapping or rule.

title: Coordinates, Lines & Graphs
coreInsight: An equation in two quantities describes coordinate pairs that satisfy a relationship, and slope measures a rate linking horizontal and vertical change.
narrativeTransition: Turn a table of related quantities into plotted points, then connect the graph to the equation and interpret slope using the rate ideas the learner already knows.
commonMisconceptions: Coordinate order can be swapped.
Axis scale does not affect interpretation.
Slope is merely visual steepness independent of units.
A graph is a drawing rather than the set of solutions to a relationship.

title: Patterns & Sequences
coreInsight: A sequence is generated by structure; good pattern reasoning identifies what remains consistent rather than merely guessing the next visible term.
narrativeTransition: Show several sequences that initially look compatible with the same guess, forcing the learner to describe a rule rather than just extrapolate a surface pattern.
commonMisconceptions: Every sequence has a constant difference.
The term number and the term value are the same quantity.
A few matching terms prove a guessed rule.
Recursive and explicit descriptions are interchangeable without translation.

title: Exponents & Roots
coreInsight: Exponents encode repeated multiplicative structure, and roots reverse powers.
narrativeTransition: Compress repeated multiplication in the same way multiplication compresses repeated addition, then reverse the process with roots.
commonMisconceptions: a^n means a times n.
Exponent rules distribute over addition.
Taking a square root means dividing by 2.
The roles of base and exponent can be interchanged.
